name: cmsisdap-sim
experiment:
# CMSIS-DAP debug probe through the native SWD stack.
#
# The default run uses the plugin's in-process SYNTHETIC probe and Cortex-M
# target, so it needs no hardware. Everything it shows (the core, the vector
# table, the registers) is simulated, not measured:
#
#   HWLAB_CMSISDAP_SIM=1 hwlab run --yes examples/cmsisdap-sim.yaml
#
# For a real probe (UNVALIDATED: the USB transports and the behaviour on real
# probes and targets have never run; no CMSIS-DAP probe was available):
#
#   hwlab devices                                  # cmsisdap/<vid>:<pid>:<serial>
#   hwlab invoke cmsisdap/<id> DebugProbe.info
#   hwlab invoke cmsisdap/<id> DebugProbe.connect
#
# and replace `device:` below. Linux needs access to the probe's usbfs node
# (v2) or hidraw node (v1), e.g. through a udev rule. The steps halt and
# reset the target, so they need --yes; nothing here writes memory or flash.
name: cmsisdap-sim
duration: 2s

devices:
  dbg:
    plugin: cmsisdap
    device: sim-cmsisdap

steps:
  - {name: probe-info, at: 100ms, device: dbg, call: DebugProbe.info}
  - {name: connect,    at: 200ms, device: dbg, call: DebugProbe.connect}
  - {name: vectors,    at: 300ms, device: dbg, call: MemoryAccess.read, args: {address: "0x0", length: 16}}
  - {name: halt,       at: 400ms, device: dbg, call: DebugProbe.halt}
  - {name: registers,  at: 500ms, device: dbg, call: DebugProbe.read_registers}
  - {name: step,       at: 600ms, device: dbg, call: DebugProbe.step}
  - {name: reset-halt, at: 700ms, device: dbg, call: DebugProbe.reset, args: {halt: true}}
  - {name: resume,     at: 800ms, device: dbg, call: DebugProbe.resume}
